reviewed_by: Opus 5 blind reviewer, re-review after the conversion gate and cm ceiling, 2026-08-13

samples_reviewed.question_text: The distance from the bench to the tree is 2 m. The distance from the gate to the tree is 1 m. Which distance is longer?
Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.
Which is longer: 7 cm or 9 cm?
Which is longer: 5 cm or 7 cm?
Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.
Which is longer: 8 cm or 5 cm?
How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.
Which is longer: 60 cm or 68 cm?
The distance from the bench to the tree is 82 m. The distance from the gate to the tree is 37 m. Which distance is longer?
The distance from the bench to the tree is 65 m. The distance from the gate to the tree is 47 m. Which distance is longer?
Which is longer: 5 cm or 6 cm?
A shoe is 20 cm long. A ruler is 15 cm long. How many cm longer is a shoe than a ruler?
Which is longer: 7 cm or 3 cm?
Measure the object. Its length is ___ m.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The compare half of the sentence is fulfilled and answerable from the stem alone: seed 44 'Which is longer: 7 cm or 9 cm?' and seed 500 'Which is longer: 60 cm or 68 cm?' carry both quantities in the text. The measure half is not answerable. Seeds 43 and 46 both render 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.' and seed 55 renders 'How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.' Neither names an object nor carries any depiction, ruler image, or scale in the sample, so nothing in the stem determines the keyed answers 1, 2 and 2; a student can only guess. Seed 603 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ m.' has the identical hole with a keyed answer of 3. Four of fourteen samples are therefore unanswerable as written, and they are exactly the samples that would have carried the verb measure.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Taking each named part separately. Compare lengths of objects: found and sound, seeds 44, 45, 50, 600, 602 and 500. Distance in meters: found, seed 42 'The distance from the bench to the tree is 2 m. The distance from the gate to the tree is 1 m.' and seeds 501 and 502. Measure lengths in centimeters: attempted at seeds 43, 46 and 55 but hollow, since 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.' gives nothing to measure. Measure lengths in meters: attempted only at seed 603, same hollow form. Using appropriate measuring tools: not found anywhere in the packet. No stem asks which tool to use, mentions a tape measure, or shows a ruler in use; seed 601 'A shoe is 20 cm long. A ruler is 15 cm long. How many cm longer is a shoe than a ruler?' names a ruler only as a measured object, not as an instrument. Two named parts are missing or non-functional.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: No item requires an operation beyond Grade 2 Quarter 2. The comparison items ask only which of two two-digit quantities is larger, as in seed 500 'Which is longer: 60 cm or 68 cm?' and seed 501 'The distance from the bench to the tree is 82 m.' The single arithmetic item, seed 601 'A shoe is 20 cm long. A ruler is 15 cm long. How many cm longer is a shoe than a ruler?', needs one subtraction within 100 keyed to 5. No multiplication, division, fractions, decimals or unit conversion between cm and m appears in any stem, and no item mixes the two units inside one comparison.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three formatters appear (mcq, cloze, read_mcq) but the fourteen samples collapse into only four stem families, one of which dominates. Six samples reuse the wording 'Which is longer: ' with only the two numbers changed (seeds 44, 45, 50, 600, 602, 500). Three reuse the identical landmark framing 'The distance from the bench to the tree is' with the same bench, gate and tree every time (seeds 42, 501, 502). Three more repeat 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.' verbatim. Only seed 601 offers a contextual word problem, and only seed 55 varies the read wording with 'How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.' The surface variety is thin for a competency that spans measuring, comparing and distance.

competency_alignment.rationale: Unit assignment matches the sentence precisely: objects are quantified in cm and landmark separations in m, as in seed 502 'The distance from the bench to the tree is 65 m. The distance from the gate to the tree is 47 m. Which distance is longer?' Two drifts. First, the clause about using appropriate measuring tools is never exercised, so the stems land short of the written scope. Second, seed 601 'How many cm longer is a shoe than a ruler?' asks for a quantified difference, which is a solve-a-problem task rather than the comparison this sentence names, and the same template appears in the sibling solve lc of this node group.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Units suit the things measured throughout, and the large seeds are plausible: seed 501 'The distance from the bench to the tree is 82 m. The distance from the gate to the tree is 37 m.' is a believable schoolyard pair, and seed 601 'A shoe is 20 cm long. A ruler is 15 cm long.' pairs objects with sensible sizes. The small end is not plausible. Seed 42 'The distance from the bench to the tree is 2 m. The distance from the gate to the tree is 1 m.' places a gate one metre from a tree, which is not a distance between landmarks. Seed 43 keys 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.' to 1 and seed 46 keys the same stem to 2, so the child is asked to measure a one or two centimetre object; seed 603 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ m.' keys 3, a three metre object with no name to make that credible.
